title: Grant proposal summary for a high school ham radio club
summary: A fictional $2,500 school-club request with a teaching plan and measurable outcomes.

blocks.heading: A radio station students can explain
blocks.body: Request: $2,500 for a one-year high-school amateur radio pilot. Students will investigate signals, build receive-only experiments, practise station logging and learn the responsibilities of licensed operation. This is a sample proposal, not an existing school’s record.

blocks.heading: From a signal on a screen to a person on the other end
blocks.body: A radio club connects circuit theory, geography and careful communication. The project begins with listening and measurement so students can participate before licensing. Any transmitting activity must follow the applicable rules and school approvals with an appropriately licensed control operator.

blocks.heading: Requested support
rows: Approved antenna, feed line and mounting
Bench learning kits and test accessories
blocks.caption: Illustrative amounts. Secure quotes and a reviewed antenna/site plan; no improvised roof access or installation near power lines.

blocks.heading: One year, three demonstrations
items: Term 1: identify a signal path and keep a reception log with frequency, mode and time.
Term 2: build and measure a low-voltage learning circuit; explain the difference between measured and predicted results.
Term 3: run a supervised demonstration and publish a short project report containing methods, observations and limits.

blocks.heading: Evidence of learning
blocks.body: Proposed targets: 12 regular participants, 10 completed signal-path explanations and 6 students ready to attempt an appropriate licence exam. Exam results are not guaranteed. The faculty sponsor records attendance and retains equipment inventory; a volunteer mentor supports technical sessions.

blocks.heading: What happens after the grant
blocks.body: The school owns the equipment. A named sponsor maintains the inventory, checks recurring costs and trains the next student officers. Renewal depends on participation and completed work, not the purchase alone.
